title: Black queer men in Southwark | BLKOUT in Southwark
metaDescription: For Black queer men in and around Southwark — Peckham, Camberwell, Bermondsey, Elephant and Castle: what's here, what's beside us, what's worth the journey, and a community-owned door into BLKOUT.

hero.heading: BLKOUT in Southwark
hero.standfirst: BLKOUT is a community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — and Southwark holds one of our history's clearest through-lines. Dr Cecil Belfield Clarke, a gay Barbadian doctor, ran his surgery on Newington Causeway for 45 years and helped found the League of Coloured Peoples. In 1992 the Black Lesbian and Gay Centre found its permanent home in a Peckham railway arch. And in November 2020, our own Assembly series asked Southwark directly: a Black queer hero — erased? Around 80,100 Black residents live in the borough. This door is for the Black queer men among them.

quiz.heading: Know your Southwark?
quiz.sub: Three questions. No prizes except the stories.

questions.q: Dr Cecil Belfield Clarke, a gay Barbadian doctor and civil rights pioneer, ran his GP surgery for 45 years at which Southwark address?
questions.reveal: 112 Newington Causeway, near Elephant and Castle — from 1920 until his retirement in 1965. He co-founded the League of Coloured Peoples in 1931 and was the only Black District Medical Officer in Britain by 1936. A blue plaque was unveiled on the site, now London South Bank University's Perry Library, in April 2023.

questions.q: In 1992, the Black Lesbian and Gay Centre found its permanent home in a converted railway arch in which Southwark neighbourhood?
questions.reveal: Peckham, on Bellenden Road — Europe's first purpose-built Black lesbian and gay centre. It ran there until 2000, and a Rainbow Plaque was unveiled on the site in February 2024.

questions.q: In November 2020, BLKOUT's own Sunday series 'Assembly' — with Southwark LGBT Network and Southwark Council — asked a pointed question about the borough. What was it?

numbers.heading: The numbers nobody counts
numbers.body: The 2021 Census counted around 80,100 Black residents in Southwark. On the estimates we publish, that's 1,800 to 2,500 Black queer men in the borough, living here right now. These are working estimates and we welcome correction. The point is the scale: we were never a niche. We were just never counted.
numbers.history:
Southwark's Black queer history runs deeper than almost any other borough's — most of it is only now being told.

Dr Cecil Belfield Clarke came to Britain from Barbados in 1914 on a scholarship to Cambridge, and in 1920 opened a GP surgery at 112 Newington Causeway, near Elephant and Castle. He served the borough there for 45 years, co-founded the League of Coloured Peoples in 1931, became Britain's only Black District Medical Officer by 1936, and later advised the newly independent government of Ghana. He was gay, and largely written out of the history he helped make — until a blue plaque went up on the site, now London South Bank University's Perry Library, in April 2023.

In 1992, the Black Lesbian and Gay Centre — founded in Haringey in 1985 — found its permanent home in a converted railway arch on Bellenden Road, Peckham: Europe's first purpose-built Black lesbian and gay centre, running until 2000. A Rainbow Plaque marks the site since February 2024.

And in November 2020, BLKOUT held our own Assembly there in spirit if not in person: a Sunday session with Southwark LGBT Network and Southwark Council, asking the borough directly — a Southwark Black queer hero, erased? It was about Dr Clarke. If you know more of this borough's story, or you were part of that 2020 Assembly, the panel below is where you tell us.

archive.intro: Southwark runs through our own writing and our own Sundays — the 2020 Assembly session on Dr Cecil Belfield Clarke among them. Those pieces are in the story archive and being brought back online; when they are, they'll be listed here.

faq.q: Where can I meet other Black queer men in Southwark?
faq.a: Start with the door on this page — you'll hear about everything as it happens. Southwark's own scene, in the directory below, is stronger than most boroughs', and BLKOUT's national community is open to you today.

faq.q: Where can I get an STI test or PrEP in Southwark?
faq.a: Sexual Health London posts free test kits and PrEP to any London address, no GP and no conversation required, and 56 Dean Street is a short ride away in Soho.

BLKOUT is one community-owned co-operative for Black queer men across the UK — with a door in every borough. We're registered in Croydon and we belong wherever our men are. We held our own Assembly session on Southwark's history in 2020.

faq.q: I'm not out. Can I still come?
faq.a: Yes. Come as you are — nobody at this door asks you to be anything first, and your business stays yours.

faq.q: Is the history on this page accurate?
faq.a: It's checked against the public record and dated so you can see when we last looked. If we've got something wrong — or missed something you were part of — the panel at the bottom is where you tell us, and the page changes.
